name: ICIP Grand Challenge on Colorectal Cancer Tumor Grading and Segmentation
description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Accurate histopathological grading of CRC is essential for prognosis and treatment planning but remains a subjective process prone to observer variability and limited by global shortages of trained pathologists. To promote automated and standardized solutions, we organized the ICIP Grand Challenge on Colorectal Cancer Tumor Grading and Segmentation using the publicly available METU CCTGS dataset. The dataset comprises 103 whole-slide images with expert pixel-level annotations for five tissue classes. Participants submitted segmentation masks via Codalab, evaluated using metrics such as macro F-score and mIoU. Among 39 participating teams, six outperformed the Swin Transformer baseline (62.92 F-score). This paper presents an overview of the challenge, dataset, and the top-performing methods
typical_sota_score: 62.92 F-score baseline; top teams exceeded this
reputation: A challenge benchmark associated with a public colorectal cancer dataset and Codalab evaluation, with active participation from multiple teams.
notes: Challenge-style benchmark on whole-slide histopathology; evaluation also used mIoU, and results depend on the specific leaderboard split and submission protocol.
